edges.description: Reproduces barrier disruption, macrophage infiltration and cochlear inflammasome activation, and shows the dependence on NLRP3.
edges.limitations: The phenotype requires an LPS challenge rather than arising spontaneously, and the allele is D301N (a NOMID/CINCA-associated variant), not the p.Arg918Gln of the human DFNA34 families. Whether the human variant behaves the same without a systemic trigger is untested.

edges.description: Both an IL-1 receptor antagonist and the NLRP3-specific inhibitor MCC950 alleviate the LPS-induced hearing loss, which is the pharmacological test of the IL-1 step.
edges.limitations: Rescue is demonstrated against an LPS-provoked phenotype, not against the slow spontaneous course seen in human DFNA34.

edges.description: Gives severe to profound hearing loss with a disorganized organ of Corti, confirming that Nlrp3 alteration alone can damage the cochlea.
edges.limitations: The course is wrong in every temporal respect: severe loss by postnatal day 20 against adult onset in humans, limited life expectancy, and a cochlear abnormality that resolves by P15 and so reads as a developmental lag rather than the progressive inflammatory injury of human DFNA34. The allele is again D301N rather than p.Arg918Gln.

nodes.description: Recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist. This is the treatment that makes the entry unusual: hearing loss was reversed or improved in affected members of the syndromic family, and improvement against natural course was seen in three probands in an independent cohort. Response is not universal - a baseline threshold worse than 60 dB and cochlear enhancement on MRI both track with poor audiologic response even when systemic symptoms settle.

evidence.reference_title: NLRP3 mutation and cochlear autoinflammation cause syndromic and nonsyndromic hearing loss DFNA34 responsive to anakinra therapy.
evidence.snippet: In family LMG446, hearing loss is accompanied by autoinflammatory signs and symptoms without serologic evidence of inflammation as part of an atypical CAPS phenotype and was reversed or improved by IL-1β blockade therapy.

nodes.description: IL-1 beta and downstream mediators increase permeability of the blood-labyrinth barrier, admitting circulating macrophages into cochlear tissue. In DFNA34 patients this is seen indirectly as pathologic enhancement of the cochlea on post-contrast MRI-FLAIR; in NLRP3-mutant mice it is measured directly, and both resident and infiltrating macrophages contribute to the resulting hearing loss.

nodes.description: Puts the CAPS-associated mutation only in the cell population this entry says matters, then challenges it with systemic LPS. It is the cleanest available test that a cochlear macrophage inflammasome is sufficient to mediate hearing loss.

Mutant NLRP3 oligomerizes and recruits ASC and pro-caspase-1 with a reduced requirement for a second activating signal. The cells that matter for this entry are the macrophage/monocyte-like cells resident in the cochlea, which express NLRP3 and carry a functional inflammasome; this was the observation that made a cochlea-only phenotype mechanistically coherent rather than merely an odd CAPS variant.

evidence.snippet: The inflammasome can indeed be activated in macrophage/monocyte-like cells of the mouse cochlea, with secretion of IL-1β.

nodes.description: The loss begins at high frequencies with a downsloping configuration and recruits low and middle frequencies with advancing age.

nodes.description: Active caspase-1 cleaves pro-IL-1 beta to mature IL-1 beta, which is secreted into the cochlear microenvironment. The human evidence that the variant is functionally activating is peripheral rather than cochlear: monocytes from affected individuals secrete IL-1 beta on priming alone, where control monocytes secrete none and require a second signal. The cochlear compartment of the same step is shown only in mouse, so the inference this node makes is that the cell-autonomous defect measured in blood monocytes is the same one operating in cochlea-resident macrophages.

evidence.reference_title: Otological aspects of NLRP3-related autoinflammatory disorder focusing on the responsiveness to anakinra.
evidence.snippet: We identified the second DNFA34 pedigree worldwide with a novel NLRP3 variant supported by in vitro analysis.

nodes.description: A heterozygous missense variant in NLRP3 - p.Arg918Gln (c.2753G>A) in the leucine-rich repeat domain in both originally reported families - lowers the activation threshold of the NLRP3 sensor. The same class of variant causes the cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes; what distinguishes DFNA34 is which tissue manifests the consequence, not the nature of the lesion.

nodes.description: Conditional mutant Nlrp3 activation in the cochlea and hematopoietic cells. Earlier mutant Nlrp3 animals died before hearing could be tested, so this is the first model in which Nlrp3-driven hearing loss is quantifiable.

Sustained cochlear autoinflammation injures the sensory epithelium of the organ of Corti and its supporting structures, producing bilateral high-frequency-predominant loss that extends to lower frequencies with age. Human cochlear histopathology is unavailable, so the cellular detail is supplied by mouse models: conditional mutant Nlrp3 expression yields severe hearing loss with a disorganized organ of Corti.

animal_models.description: Gives severe to profound hearing loss with a disorganized organ of Corti, confirming that Nlrp3 alteration alone can damage the cochlea.

evidence.reference_title: Auditory Phenotype and Histopathologic Findings of a Mutant Nlrp3 Expression Mouse Model.
evidence.snippet: The hematoxylin-eosin sections of Nlrp3 D301NneoR/+; Gfi1 Cre/+ mice cochleae at P12 exhibited a disorganized organ of Corti between the outer hair cells/supporting Deiters' cells and basilar membrane compared with the normal phenotype mice, leading to a collapsed Nuel's space.
